title: The Blind Mans Theory of the Science of Math
author: Korbey, Holly
summary: The science of reading toppled balanced literacy and ushered in evidence-based practice. Yet few educators see that the same research principles apply to math, science, and all learning. Like the Biblical blind man miraculously healed, people would rather deny what's plainly in front of them than change entrenched practices. This willful ignorance keeps millions of students failing in math despite the existence of evidence-based instructional methods.
points: The science of reading success should trigger parallel reforms in math instruction, but it hasnt.
Evidence-based learning principles apply to all subjects, not just reading.
Many educators seem willfully blind to parallel breakthroughs that could help struggling math students.
Newer teachers, trained in balanced literacy, lack the intuitive sense of what actually works that older teachers had.
Professional development in science-based instruction is becoming ubiquitous but still not universally required.
quotes: I thought people would quickly make a crucial leap, an important connection that teaching and learning has a body of evidence behind it.
Some who watched the science of reading change how reading was being taught can't see how similar ideas apply to math.
Teachers from previous generations could juxtapose their experience as students with new progressive methods and see something was amiss.
Until colleges shift (which could take years), it's imperative professional development be grounded in proven, research-backed methods.” Archived from Bell Ringers on May 2, 2026 by Tim.
